These results shift attention toward controlled endpoint response, carefully qualified loading associations, and reproducibility checks.","batch_rationale":"The 32 choices cover 16 already observed molecules through compact experiments with specific learning questions. m81 and m33 address persistent completion failures and loading interactions. The sulfur/methoxy ketones test the revised endpoint-specific interpretation of the recent substituent comparison. The aldehyde and amino-ester rows locate early transitions, plateaus and possible minima using measured anchors. m29, m38 and m197 test conspicuous strong-eluent predictions in distinct structural environments, while the m73 pair checks reproducibility in an inconsistent region. m75 and m39 extend early-response coverage to related neutral multiacceptor families with useful later anchors. Multiple rows per molecule are justified by controlled comparisons; duplicate candidate tuples are otherwise avoided. Quantile spans and CW distance are secondary diagnostics from the single predictor, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and elution interval width is treated as a target relationship rather than uncertainty. The batch is intended to improve generalization across the Row-distribution by supplying transferable structure-ratio-loading relationships and clarifying misleading local patterns, without selecting for maximal retention or chromatographic performance."}
